meta.title: Snow Removal in Goodrich, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Snow plowing in Goodrich, MI: Grand Scapes clears long drives off gravel and county roads with our own trucks, plus walks, steps and salt where people walk.

hero.title: Long drives, **plowed wide.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes plows Goodrich driveways with our own trucks, from short village drives to long ones off Atlas Township gravel roads. Walks and steps get cleared to the concrete and salted.

local.title: Long drives off **gravel county roads.**
local.intro: Around Goodrich, the main snow job is distance. Many Atlas Township homes sit far back on lots of two acres or more, often off a gravel road, and the road out front is on the county's plow list, not the township's. In the village, drives are shorter and there are sidewalks to think about.

points.title: Gravel roads come last
points.body: Local roads around Goodrich belong to the Genesee County Road Commission, and its winter list puts unpaved local roads and subdivision streets at the end, without overtime crews.

points.title: Edges, culverts and mailboxes
points.body: On a long drive, the edges, the culvert and the mailbox disappear under the first real snowfall. Marking them in the fall shows the plow where the lawn stops and the ditch starts.

points.title: Township sidewalks
points.body: Atlas Township's sidewalk ordinance says sidewalks must be kept clear of ice and snow, and that snow must not be piled where it blocks a sidewalk, a road or a driver's view. An HOA may take that job on for its subdivision.

points.title: Snow kept off the road
points.body: State law forbids depositing snow, ice or slush on any roadway. Snow from the drive gets stacked on your own ground, away from the road and the sight line where you pull out.

logistics.title: How snow removal works on a Goodrich drive.
body: Each season starts with a fall visit from Rob. He looks at the length and width of the drive, where snow can be pushed and stacked, the turnaround by the garage, the walks and steps, and anything hidden at the edges.

Through the winter, the drive gets plowed with our own trucks, and walks and steps are shoveled to the concrete. Salt goes where people walk and where cars stop. In the village, ask about the sidewalk along the street, and check with the village office on its rules.

faq.q: Do you plow driveways in Goodrich, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes plows driveways in the Village of Goodrich and around Atlas Township with our own trucks, and we clear and salt walks and steps. Estimates are free.

faq.q: When does the county plow gravel roads near Goodrich?
faq.a: After the bigger roads. The Genesee County Road Commission plows by traffic volume, and unpaved local roads and subdivision streets come last, with no overtime on either. After a big storm, a gravel road can stay snow covered well after your drive is clear.

faq.q: Will the county plow knock over my mailbox?
faq.a: Heavy snow off a county plow can. The Road Commission asks owners to check their mailbox and post every fall and replace anything weak. If its plow damages a mailbox, its crews replace it with a standard one once the roads are cleared.

faq.q: Do I have to clear the sidewalk in Atlas Township?
faq.a: Yes, if one runs along your property. The township's sidewalk ordinance puts sidewalk upkeep on the property owner, including keeping it free of ice and snow, though an HOA can take that on. In the Village of Goodrich, ask the village office what applies on your street.

faq.q: How do your snow packages work?
faq.a: Each one is quoted for your property. Grand Scapes has residential and commercial snow removal and salting packages, and Rob talks through what you want cleared and salted before he prices it. The details depend on the drive, so he explains them in person.
